name: Bhili
confidence_why: The only description of Bhili that mentions stress, Vyas's 1967 field dissertation on the Central and North dialects, states for both that stress is not distinctive and gives no placement rule, while Thompson 1895, Grierson 1907 and the Linguistic Survey of India volumes on Varli (2003) and Wagdi (2011) say nothing about stress, so the record rests on one unopposed first-hand source.
catalog_citation: Vyas, Yogendra Dhirubhai. 1967. A linguistic study of Bhili dialects: a descriptive study of Central and North Bhili. PhD thesis, Gujarat University (guide P. B. Pandit). xvii+362 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/49002; Glottolog hh:553051.
catalog_locator: Part I Central Bhili, ch. 1 Phonemics, sec. e 'Syllable structure', thesis p. 28; Part II North Bhili, sec. e 'Syllable structure', thesis p. 133
catalog_quote: p. 28 (Central Bhili): "Stress is not distinctive. Syllable division can be made in terms of phonetic criteria. We can segment sequences at the point of closest stricture." p. 133 (North Bhili): "Stress is not distinctive. Syllable division clearly be made in terms of phonetic criteria. We can cut sequences at the point of closest stricture."

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is stated to be non-contrastive (not phonemic) in both Central Bhili (Jhalod, Panch Mahals) and North Bhili (Dungarpur); the author gives no rule for where phonetic prominence falls, and vowel-length allophony is tied to nasalisation, word-final position and monosyllables rather than to stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no positional rule is given at all.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement made in the syllable-structure section of a phonemic analysis of elicited words/utterances; word-level phonemics, no phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Vyas 1967) describes two field varieties: 'Central Bhili' = speech of Sukhsar near Jhalod, Panch Mahals (now Dahod district), Gujarat -- the Mahikantha-Panchmahals variety Grierson called 'standard Bhili' -- and 'North Bhili' = villages around Dungarpur, Rajasthan, i.e. the Vagad area whose Bhil speech the Census/LSI-Rajasthan volume and Glottolog treat as Wagdi (wagd1238). Glottolog files Vyas 1967 under bhil1251, but Glottolog's bhil1251 map point (20.85N 73.96E, Nashik district, Maharashtra) lies far south of both field sites; the Dangs/Khandesh-side Bhili nearest that point is described by Kulkarni 1976 (not accessible). The identical stress sentence is given for both of Vyas's varieties. Other files saved here describe Wagdi (LSI Rajasthan 2011, wagd1238) and Varli (LSI Dadra & Nagar Haveli 2003, varl1238), not Bhili proper.

sources.note: Central Bhili (Sukhsar/Jhalod, Panch Mahals), ch.1 sec. e Syllable structure, p. 28: 'Stress is not distinctive. Syllable division can be made in terms of phonetic criteria.' Same sentence for North Bhili (Dungarpur), p. 133. No statement of where stress falls; vowel length allophony (pp. 7-10, 111-116) is conditioned by nasalisation, final position and monosyllables, not stress. No other mention of stress/accent in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent all chapters).

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 3254.104)
sources.note: Preface only: 'Besides the actual change of letter, there is also to be noted a difference in pronunciation. The tone and the accent are not quite the same in places separated by, say, a score of miles' (illustrated with vowel-quality differences in Kotra); also notes no accents (length marks) were printed for want of type. No stress rule. Variety: Bhili of Rajputana/Mahikantha (Kherwara mission area).
Phonology section gives consonant/vowel tables only (sourced to Vyas 1967 and Phillips 2012); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mukherjee, Sibasis. 2011. Wagdi [described as the 'Wagdi variety of Bhili/Bhilodi']. In: Linguistic Survey of India: Rajasthan, Part I, pp. 406-463. Kolkata: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 Suprasegmental phonemes (p. 412) lists only vowel length ('Length is not phonemic here.. Vowels occurring in monosyllabic words are uniformly long') and nasalization; sec. 2.7 Syllable has no stress statement. Silent on stress. Describes Wagdi as spoken by Bhils of Dungarpur/Banswara (wagd1238), the volume has no separate Bhili chapter.

sources.citation: Koul, M. K. & Pattanayak, Ranjita (Language Division). 2003. Linguistic Survey of India: Dadra and Nagar Haveli [Varli grammar; Glottolog hh:319895 lists it as Ahirwal 2003 'Varli' under bhil1251]. Kolkata: ORGI.
sources.note: Phonology ch. (vol. p. 32 ff.): '47 segmental phonemes and two supra-segmental phonemes.. Nasalization and length'; Suprasegmentals section treats only nasalisation and length. Silent on stress. Language described is Varli (varl1238), classified by the Census under Bhili/Bhilodi -- not Bhili proper.

tone.summary: No mention of tone, pitch or word stress in the 197-page survey report. The IPA key (Appendix B) has only nasalisation, length and centralisation diacritics; the wordlists are field transcriptions without phonological analysis (p. 74). 'Accent' occurs only in Hindi proficiency-level descriptions.
